Day 19 of 100 · AWS Networking Foundations

AWS Config

#100DaysOfCloudAndSecurityAWS Networking FoundationsTopic verified by artifact

AWS Config records resource configuration state and can evaluate whether resources match defined compliance rules.

Architecture / mental model

AWS resources → configuration recorder → configuration history / rules → compliance findings

How it works

AWS Config answers a different question from an activity log: what did the configuration of this resource look like, how did it change and does it currently satisfy a rule?

Managed or custom rules can evaluate properties such as encryption, public exposure or required configuration. Compliance state is useful only when findings have owners and remediation paths.

Configuration history is especially useful during incident review because it helps connect a current misconfiguration to when the resource state changed.

Hands-on reference

aws configservice describe-configuration-recorders
aws configservice describe-compliance-by-config-rule

Verification

Confirm recording is enabled for intended resource types/Regions, then inspect a known resource's configuration timeline and rule evaluation.

Field note / gotcha

AWS Config is not CloudTrail. Config focuses on resource configuration state; CloudTrail records account/API activity.

Security considerations

Protect Config destinations and roles, choose rules that map to real controls and avoid treating a green compliance dashboard as proof an application is secure.

What I learned

Security improves when configuration drift becomes observable instead of discoverable only after an outage or audit.
